body:
The Prevent All Cigarette Trafficking Act, usually called the PACT Act, was amended by legislation signed in December 2020. Its provisions covering e-cigarettes and vaping products took effect on March 27, 2021. For anyone buying vapor products online, the law explains several things that can seem strange at first: why parcels need an adult signature, why they carry a special label, why some carriers do not handle them and why sellers must follow tax and licensing rules. This guide explains what the PACT Act covers, how it affects shipping, signatures, labels and taxes, what it means for you as a buyer and where to find more. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so confirm requirements with official sources.

## What it is
The PACT Act was first passed in 2009 to address the illegal trafficking of cigarettes and to make remote sales of tobacco products subject to similar rules as sales in stores. The December 2020 amendments extended its provisions to e-cigarettes and vaping products, with a start date of March 27, 2021. The law treats vaping products similarly to cigarettes for remote sales. That includes how they are shipped, taxed and delivered.

## Shipping limits
One of the best-known effects is that the U.S. Postal Service may not carry vaping products, so sellers use other carriers. Some carriers have also limited what they accept, and rules and carrier policies can change, which can lead to interruptions in some areas. We use regional carriers that handle vapor shipments. That is part of why delivery times vary by region and why our shipping policy gives ranges. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and our [shipping policy](/shipping/).

## Adult signature
Every delivery must be signed for by an adult aged 21 or older, who must show valid government-issued photo ID. This applies in every state to every parcel containing vapor products. It is the single feature of the law that customers notice most, because it means the parcel cannot be left at the door. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/).

## Labeling
Parcels must carry a label stating that federal law requires payment of applicable excise taxes and compliance with licensing and tax-stamping obligations. The label is small and factual. It does not name the products inside, and it is a legal requirement for remote vape shipments. See [discreet packaging](/blog/discreet-packaging-what-to-expect/) for what your parcel looks like.

## Taxes and licensing
Sellers must register and comply with state and local licensing and tax rules. Some states tax vape products, in different ways, and sellers may collect those taxes. The law also requires sellers to report certain sales to state tax authorities in some cases. The details are complex, and they differ by state, which is why a seller may be unable to ship certain products to certain places. See [vape taxes by state](/blog/vape-taxes-by-state-overview/) and [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## What it means for you
You may see delivery rules and restrictions that did not exist for older orders. You may need to be present to sign, and you may find that some products cannot be shipped to your area. Our own summary is on the [PACT Act FAQ](/pact-act/) page, and details on shipping are in the [shipping policy](/shipping/). You are responsible for knowing the rules where you live, and for making sure that buying, receiving and using these products is lawful for you.

## What it means for sellers
A seller that ships vapor products must verify age, use adult-signature delivery, label parcels, register with the relevant authorities and comply with tax and licensing rules. A seller that does not may face serious penalties. That is why you should be cautious of any seller that offers to skip the signature or the label, or to ship without age checks. A seller that ignores these rules is ignoring the law, and your purchase may be at risk.

## Common questions about the law
### Why can't the Postal Service deliver vapes?
The law restricts the mailing of vaping products, with limited exceptions, so sellers use private carriers. Policies of some private carriers have also changed over time.

### Why do I need to show ID?
The law requires adult signature confirmation. Showing government-issued photo ID is how the delivery employee confirms that the signer is 21 or older.

### Why is there a warning label on the parcel?
The law requires parcels containing vaping products to carry a statement about excise taxes and licensing and tax-stamping obligations.

### Does the law apply to me as a buyer?
It applies mainly to sellers and carriers, but it shapes what you experience: signature, labels, delivery restrictions and availability.

### Will the rules change?
They can. Carriers, states and regulators update their rules, so check official sources and our policies for the latest.

## How this connects with our service
We follow the rules that apply to us, and we expect customers to follow theirs. That means adult signature on every parcel, compliant labels, delivery with carriers that handle vapor shipments, and cancelling orders that cannot be delivered lawfully. See [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/) and our [terms](/terms/).

## Not legal advice
This article summarizes publicly known features of the law in plain language. It is not legal advice, and it may not cover every detail or recent change. Rules differ by state and city, and they change. Confirm requirements with official sources, such as federal and state agencies, and ask a qualified professional about your own situation. If you have a question about how a rule affects an order with us, ask through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Related reading
Read [the FDA and vaping products](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/), [how ordering works](/blog/how-ordering-works/) and [how to become a wholesale customer](/blog/how-to-become-a-wholesale-customer/) if you run a shop. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A brief timeline
The PACT Act became law in 2009 and targeted illegal cigarette trafficking. It was amended by a law signed in December 2020, which brought e-cigarettes and vaping products within its remote-sale provisions, effective March 27, 2021. After that date, carriers and sellers had to adjust: the Postal Service could no longer carry vaping products, adult signature became a requirement for deliveries of vapor products and sellers had to meet the registration, reporting and tax obligations that apply to remote sellers. Many sellers changed how they ship, and some customers noticed longer delivery times as a result of new routes and carriers.

## What this looks like from the customer's side
You place an order, and the seller ships it with a carrier that handles vapor shipments. The parcel carries the required label. When it arrives, an adult signs and shows ID. If you are not available, the carrier tries again and may return the parcel. If the seller cannot lawfully ship to your area, it cancels the order. At each step, the law is at work, even if the process feels slower than an ordinary online purchase.

## Questions to ask any online seller
- Do you require adult signature on delivery?
- Do you label parcels as the law requires?
- Do you verify age and cancel orders that cannot be delivered lawfully?
- Do you make health or regulatory claims that you cannot support?
- Do you explain your shipping, returns and compliance clearly?

A seller that answers yes to the first four and clearly to the last is likely taking the rules seriously. A seller that is vague or dismissive is a warning sign.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does the PACT Act mean I pay extra taxes?
The law requires sellers to meet tax and licensing obligations. Any tax that applies to your order is shown in your order summary before you pay. Rates and rules differ by state.

### Can a seller ignore the PACT Act?
A seller that ships vapor products must follow it. A seller that ignores it may face penalties, and a parcel from such a seller may be refused by carriers or seized. That is a good reason to buy from a seller that explains its compliance.

### Why did delivery change after 2021?
After the law took effect, sellers moved to carriers that handle vapor shipments, and routes and times changed. That is one reason delivery to some regions takes longer than it once did.

### Do I have to do anything under the PACT Act as a buyer?
You need to be 21 or older, be available to sign with ID and follow the laws where you live. You do not file anything yourself.

### Where can I read the law itself?
Official sources, such as federal agencies and government publications, publish the text and guidance. Use them if you need the exact wording for a decision.

### Why this matters when you compare sellers
Sellers that follow the PACT Act spend time and money on compliance, which can show up as longer delivery estimates, adult-signature requirements and parcel labels. Sellers that skip these steps may seem faster and simpler, but they take risks that can end up with you, such as seized parcels or cancelled orders. When you compare sellers, a clear explanation of how they ship, label and verify age is a good sign. See our [shipping policy](/shipping/) and [PACT Act FAQ](/pact-act/) for how we handle it.
